sanskrit: yayātir devayānyāṃ tu putrāv ajanayan nṛpaḥ yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva śakraviṣṇū ivāparau
english: King Yayāti begot two sons upon Devayānī — Yadu and Turvasu — who were like Indra and Viṣṇu themselves.

sanskrit: tasmād eva tu rājarṣeḥ śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca trīn kumārān ajījanat
english: From that same royal sage, Śarmiṣṭhā the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan gave birth to three princes — Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāle tu kasmiṃś cid devayānī śucismitā yayātisahitā rājan nirjagāma mahāvanam
english: Then on a certain occasion, O king, the fair-smiling Devayānī went out into the great forest accompanied by Yayāti.

sanskrit: dadarśa ca tadā tatra kumārān devarūpiṇaḥ krīḍamānān suviśrabdhān vismitā cedam abravīt
english: There she saw boys beautiful as gods playing at their ease, and astonished she said this:

sanskrit: kasyaite dārakā rājan devaputropamāḥ śubhāḥ varcasā rūpataś caiva sadṛśā me matās tava
english: "Whose are these children, O king, auspicious and resembling sons of gods? In radiance and form they seem to me like your own."

sanskrit: evaṃ pṛṣṭvā tu rājānaṃ kumārān paryapṛcchata kiṃnāmadheyagotro vaḥ putrakā brāhmaṇaḥ pitā vibrūta me yathātathyaṃ śrotum icchāmi taṃ hy aham
english: Having questioned the king thus, she then questioned the boys: "What are your names and lineage, little ones? Who is your brahmin father? Tell me truly — I wish to know him."

sanskrit: te 'darśayan pradeśinyā tam eva nṛpasattamam śarmiṣṭhāṃ mātaraṃ caiva tasyācakhyuś ca dārakāḥ
english: The boys pointed with their forefingers to that very best of kings, and they named Śarmiṣṭhā as their mother.

sanskrit: ity uktvā sahitās te tu rājānam upacakramuḥ nābhyanandata tān rājā devayānyās tadāntike rudantas te 'tha śarmiṣṭhām abhyayur bālakās tataḥ
english: Having spoken so, they went together toward the king; but the king did not welcome them in Devayānī's presence. Then, weeping, the boys ran to Śarmiṣṭhā.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu teṣāṃ bālānāṃ praṇayaṃ pārthivaṃ prati buddhvā ca tattvato devī śarmiṣṭhām idam abravīt
english: Seeing the boys' affection toward the king and understanding the truth of it, the noble lady spoke thus to Śarmiṣṭhā:

sanskrit: madadhīnā satī kasmād akārṣīr vipriyaṃ mama tam evāsuradharmaṃ tvam āsthitā na bibheṣi kim
english: "Though you were under my authority, why have you done me this wrong? You have followed the ways of the asuras — do you not fear?"

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca yad uktam ṛṣir ity eva tat satyaṃ cāruhāsini nyāyato dharmataś caiva carantī na bibhemi te
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "What was said was that he was a sage — that is the truth, O lovely-smiling one. Acting rightly and in accordance with dharma, I do not fear you."

sanskrit: yadā tvayā vṛto rājā vṛta eva tadā mayā sakhībhartā hi dharmeṇa bhartā bhavati śobhane
english: "When the king was chosen by you, he was then chosen by me as well — for a friend's husband is, by dharma, a husband, O beautiful one."

sanskrit: pūjyāsi mama mānyā ca jyeṣṭhā śreṣṭhā ca brāhmaṇī tvatto 'pi me pūjyatamo rājarṣiḥ kiṃ na vettha tat
english: "You are my revered and honored elder — a brahmin woman, the most excellent. Yet even above you, the royal sage is most worthy of my veneration — do you not know that?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā tasyās tato vākyaṃ devayāny abravīd idam rājan nādyeha vatsyāmi vipriyaṃ me kṛtaṃ tvayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing her words, Devayānī then said: "O king, I will not stay here any longer — you have done me wrong."

sanskrit: sahasotpatitāṃ śyāmāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ sāśrulocanām tvaritaṃ sakāśaṃ kāvyasya prasthitāṃ vyathitas tadā
english: Seeing the dark-complexioned woman suddenly rise with tears in her eyes, setting out swiftly toward Kāvya's abode, the king was then distressed.

sanskrit: anuvavrāja saṃbhrāntaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sāntvayan nṛpaḥ nyavartata na caiva sma krodhasaṃraktalocanā
english: Agitated, the king followed behind her, trying to soothe her — but she, her eyes reddened with anger, did not turn back.

sanskrit: avibruvantī kiṃ cit tu rājānaṃ cārulocanā acirād iva saṃprāptā kāvyasyośanaso 'ntikam
english: Without saying anything to the king, the lovely-eyed woman swiftly arrived at the presence of Kāvya Uśanas.

sanskrit: sā tu dṛṣṭvaiva pitaram abhivādyāgrataḥ sthitā anantaraṃ yayātis tu pūjayām āsa bhārgavam
english: Seeing her father, she paid her respects and stood before him; and thereupon Yayāti also honored the Bhārgava sage.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca adharmeṇa jito dharmaḥ pravṛttam adharottaram śarmiṣṭhayātivṛttāsmi duhitrā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: Devayānī said: "Dharma has been defeated by adharma; a descent into wrong has begun. I have been transgressed against by Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan."

sanskrit: trayo 'syāṃ janitāḥ putrā rājñānena yayātinā durbhagāyā mama dvau tu putrau tāta bravīmi te
english: "Three sons have been fathered upon her by this king Yayāti, while upon me, the ill-fortuned one, only two sons — this I tell you, father."

sanskrit: dharmajña iti vikhyāta eṣa rājā bhṛgūdvaha atikrāntaś ca maryādāṃ kāvyaitat kathayāmi te
english: "This king, renowned as a knower of dharma, O scion of Bhṛgu, has transgressed the bounds of propriety — this, O Kāvya, I tell you."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca jarāṃ prāpya yayātis tu svapuraṃ prāpya caiva ha putraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ variṣṭhaṃ ca yadum ity abravīd vacaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having obtained old age and having returned to his own city, Yayāti spoke these words to his eldest and most excellent son Yadu:

sanskrit: jarā valī ca māṃ tāta palitāni ca paryaguḥ kāvyasyośanasaḥ śāpān na ca tṛpto 'smi yauvane
english: "Old age, wrinkles, and white hairs have overtaken me, my son, by the curse of Kāvya Uśanas, and I am not yet satisfied with youth."

sanskrit: tvaṃ yado pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha yauvanena tvadīyena careyaṃ viṣayān aham
english: "You, Yadu, take up this affliction of old age; with your youth let me enjoy the pleasures of the senses."

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu punas te yauvanaṃ tv aham dattvā svaṃ pratipatsyāmi pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha
english: "When a full thousand years have passed, I will give back your youth to you and resume my own affliction of old age."

sanskrit: yadur uvāca sitaśmaśruśirā dīno jarayā śithilīkṛtaḥ valīsaṃtatagātraś ca durdarśo durbalaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Yadu said: "With white beard and white hair, wretched, loosened by old age, with wrinkles covering every limb, unsightly, feeble, emaciated —

sanskrit: aśaktaḥ kāryakaraṇe paribhūtaḥ sa yauvanaiḥ sahopajīvibhiś caiva tāṃ jarāṃ nābhikāmaye
english: "— incapable of action, scorned by the young and by dependents alike, such old age I do not desire."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yat tvaṃ me hṛdayāj jāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi tasmād arājyabhāk tāta prajā te vai bhaviṣyati
english: Yayāti said: "Because you, born from my heart, do not give me your youth, your progeny, my son, shall not partake of kingship."

sanskrit: turvaso pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha yauvanena careyaṃ vai viṣayāṃs tava putraka
english: "Turvasu, take up this affliction of old age; with your youth I will indeed enjoy the pleasures of the senses, my son."

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu punar dāsyāmi yauvanam svaṃ caiva pratipatsyāmi pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha
english: "When a full thousand years have passed, I will give back your youth and I myself will resume the affliction of old age."

sanskrit: turvasur uvāca na kāmaye jarāṃ tāta kāmabhogapraṇāśinīm balarūpāntakaraṇīṃ buddhiprāṇavināśinīm
english: Turvasu said: "I do not desire old age, father — it destroys the enjoyment of desires, it ends strength and beauty, it ruins intellect and vital breath."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yat tvaṃ me hṛdayāj jāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi tasmāt prajā samucchedaṃ turvaso tava yāsyati
english: Yayāti said: "Because you, born from my heart, do not give me your youth, your lineage, O Turvasu, shall come to complete extinction."

sanskrit: saṃkīrṇācāradharmeṣu pratilomacareṣu ca piśitāśiṣu cāntyeṣu mūḍha rājā bhaviṣyasi
english: "Among those of mixed conduct and dharma, among those who act contrary to social order, among flesh-eaters and outcastes, you fool, shall you be a king."

sanskrit: gurudāraprasakteṣu tiryagyonigateṣu ca paśudharmiṣu pāpeṣu mleccheṣu prabhaviṣyasi
english: "Among those addicted to their elders' wives, among those fallen into animal wombs, among the sinful who follow the ways of beasts, among the mlecchas, shall you hold sway."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ sa turvasuṃ śaptvā yayātiḥ sutam ātmanaḥ śarmiṣṭhāyāḥ sutaṃ druhyum idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus cursed Turvasu, Yayāti spoke these words to his own son Druhyu, the son of Śarmiṣṭhā:

sanskrit: druhyo tvaṃ pratipadyasva varṇarūpavināśinīm jarāṃ varṣasahasraṃ me yauvanaṃ svaṃ dadasva ca
english: "Druhyu, take up this old age that destroys complexion and form; give me your youth for a thousand years."

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu pratidāsyāmi yauvanam svaṃ cādāsyāmi bhūyo 'haṃ pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha
english: "When a full thousand years have passed, I will give back your youth and I myself will once again take up the affliction of old age."

sanskrit: druhyur uvāca na gajaṃ na rathaṃ nāśvaṃ jīrṇo bhuṅkte na ca striyam vāgbhaṅgaś cāsya bhavati taj jarāṃ nābhikāmaye
english: Druhyu said: "An old man enjoys neither elephant, nor chariot, nor horse, nor woman — his speech too becomes broken. Therefore I do not desire that old age."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yat tvaṃ me hṛdayāj jāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi tasmād druhyo priyaḥ kāmo na te saṃpatsyate kva cit
english: Yayāti said: "Because you, born from my heart, do not give me your youth, O Druhyu, your cherished desires shall nowhere be fulfilled."

sanskrit: uḍupaplavasaṃtāro yatra nityaṃ bhaviṣyati arājā bhojaśabdaṃ tvaṃ tatrāvāpsyasi sānvayaḥ
english: "In a land where crossing is always only by raft and float, without a king, you and your descendants shall bear the name of Bhoja."

sanskrit: ano tvaṃ pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha ekaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu careyaṃ yauvanena te
english: "Anu, take up this affliction of old age; for one thousand years let me enjoy with your youth."

sanskrit: anur uvāca jīrṇaḥ śiśuvad ādatte 'kāle 'nnam aśucir yathā na juhoti ca kāle 'gniṃ tāṃ jarāṃ nābhikāmaye
english: Anu said: "An old man takes food like a child, at unseasonable times, like one impure; he does not offer into the sacred fire at the proper hour. That old age I do not desire."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yat tvaṃ me hṛdayāj jāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi jarādoṣas tvayokto 'yaṃ tasmāt tvaṃ pratipatsyase
english: Yayāti said: "Because you, born from my heart, do not give me your youth, the very fault of old age you have named — that you shall receive."

sanskrit: prajāś ca yauvanaprāptā vinaśiṣyanty ano tava agnipraskandanaparas tvaṃ cāpy evaṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: "And your offspring, O Anu, shall perish upon reaching youth; and you yourself shall likewise be devoted to neglecting the sacred fire."

sanskrit: pūro tvaṃ me priyaḥ putras tvaṃ varīyān bhaviṣyasi jarā valī ca me tāta palitāni ca paryaguḥ kāvyasyośanasaḥ śāpān na ca tṛpto 'smi yauvane
english: "Pūru, you are my beloved son; you shall be the greatest. Old age, wrinkles, and white hair have overtaken me, my son, by the curse of Kāvya Uśanas, and I am not satisfied with youth."

sanskrit: pūro tvaṃ pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha kaṃ cit kālaṃ careyaṃ vai viṣayān vayasā tava
english: "Pūru, take up this affliction of old age; for some time let me truly enjoy the pleasures of the senses with your youthful vigor."

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu pratidāsyāmi yauvanam svaṃ caiva pratipatsyāmi pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha
english: "When a full thousand years have passed, I will give back your youth, and I myself will resume the affliction of old age."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca pūruḥ pitaram añjasā yathāttha māṃ mahārāja tat kariṣyāmi te vacaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Pūru replied to his father straightforwardly: "As you have told me, O great king, so I will carry out your words."

sanskrit: pratipatsyāmi te rājan pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha gṛhāṇa yauvanaṃ mattaś cara kāmān yathepsitān
english: "I will take up from you the affliction of old age, O king. Take my youth and enjoy desires as you wish."

sanskrit: jarayāhaṃ praticchanno vayorūpadharas tava yauvanaṃ bhavate dattvā cariṣyāmi yathāttha mām
english: "Covered by old age, bearing your form of age, having given my youth to you, I will conduct myself as you have directed me."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca pūro prīto 'smi te vatsa prītaś cedaṃ dadāmi te sarvakāmasamṛddhā te prajā rājye bhaviṣyati
english: Yayāti said: "Pūru, I am pleased with you, my child; and pleased, I give you this: your progeny in the kingdom shall be endowed with fulfillment of all desires."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pauraveṇātha vayasā yayātir nahuṣātmajaḥ prītiyukto nṛpaśreṣṭhaś cacāra viṣayān priyān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, with the youth of the Paurava, Yayāti the son of Nahuṣa, delighted, that best of kings, pursued his beloved pleasures.

sanskrit: yathākāmaṃ yathotsāhaṃ yathākālaṃ yathāsukham dharmāviruddhān rājendro yathārhati sa eva hi
english: As he desired, with all his energy, in due season and according to his happiness, the lord of kings enjoyed pleasures unopposed to dharma, as was fitting for him.

sanskrit: devān atarpayad yajñaiḥ śrāddhais tadvat pitṝn api dīnān anugrahair iṣṭaiḥ kāmaiś ca dvijasattamān
english: He gratified the gods with sacrifices, and likewise the ancestors with śrāddha offerings; the needy with desired gifts and boons; and the best of the twice-born with desired goods.

sanskrit: atithīn annapānaiś ca viśaś ca paripālanaiḥ ānṛśaṃsyena śūdrāṃś ca dasyūn saṃnigraheṇa ca
english: He honored guests with food and drink, the commoners with protection, the śūdras with kindness, and suppressed bandits with firm restraint.

sanskrit: dharmeṇa ca prajāḥ sarvā yathāvad anurañjayan yayātiḥ pālayām āsa sākṣād indra ivāparaḥ
english: Delighting all his subjects properly with righteousness, Yayāti protected them like a second Indra himself.

sanskrit: sa rājā siṃhavikrānto yuvā viṣayagocaraḥ avirodhena dharmasya cacāra sukham uttamam
english: That king, bold as a lion, youthful, roaming through the field of pleasures, pursued the highest happiness without transgressing dharma.

sanskrit: sa saṃprāpya śubhān kāmāṃs tṛptaḥ khinnaś ca pārthivaḥ kālaṃ varṣasahasrāntaṃ sasmāra manujādhipaḥ
english: Having obtained auspicious pleasures, satisfied and yet wearied, the lord of men, that ruler of earth, recalled the time — the end of a thousand years.

sanskrit: parisaṃkhyāya kālajñaḥ kalāḥ kāṣṭhāś ca vīryavān pūrṇaṃ matvā tataḥ kālaṃ pūruṃ putram uvāca ha
english: Reckoning up the moments and the divisions of time, that knower of time, that valiant one, judged the period complete and spoke to his son Pūru:

sanskrit: yathākāmaṃ yathotsāhaṃ yathākālam ariṃdama sevitā viṣayāḥ putra yauvanena mayā tava
english: "As I desired, with full energy, and in due season, O subduer of foes, pleasures have been enjoyed by me, my son, with your youth."

sanskrit: pūro prīto 'smi bhadraṃ te gṛhāṇedaṃ svayauvanam rājyaṃ caiva gṛhāṇedaṃ tvaṃ hi me priyakṛt sutaḥ
english: "Pūru, I am pleased with you — blessings upon you. Take back this your own youth, and take also this kingdom — for you are the son who has done me pleasure."

sanskrit: pratipede jarāṃ rājā yayātir nāhuṣas tadā yauvanaṃ pratipede ca pūruḥ svaṃ punar ātmanaḥ
english: Then King Yayāti the son of Nahuṣa resumed old age, and Pūru recovered his own youth once again.

sanskrit: abhiṣektukāmaṃ nṛpatiṃ pūruṃ putraṃ kanīyasam brāhmaṇapramukhā varṇā idaṃ vacanam abruvan
english: When the king wished to consecrate Pūru, his youngest son, the four estates headed by the brahmins spoke these words:

sanskrit: kathaṃ śukrasya naptāraṃ devayānyāḥ sutaṃ prabho jyeṣṭhaṃ yadum atikramya rājyaṃ pūroḥ pradāsyasi
english: "How, O lord, will you give the kingdom to Pūru, passing over the eldest, Yadu — the grandson of Śukra and son of Devayānī?"

sanskrit: yadur jyeṣṭhas tava suto jātas tam anu turvasuḥ śarmiṣṭhāyāḥ suto druhyus tato 'nuḥ pūrur eva ca
english: "Yadu was born your eldest son; after him Turvasu; Śarmiṣṭhā's son Druhyu came next, then Anu, and only then Pūru."

sanskrit: kathaṃ jyeṣṭhān atikramya kanīyān rājyam arhati etat saṃbodhayāmas tvāṃ dharmaṃ tvam anupālaya
english: "How can the youngest deserve the kingdom, passing over the elders? We set this before you — uphold dharma."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca brāhmaṇapramukhā varṇāḥ sarve śṛṇvantu me vacaḥ jyeṣṭhaṃ prati yathā rājyaṃ na deyaṃ me kathaṃ cana
english: Yayāti said: "Let all the estates, headed by the brahmins, hear my words: as to the eldest, the kingdom is in no way to be given by me to him."

sanskrit: mama jyeṣṭhena yadunā niyogo nānupālitaḥ pratikūlaḥ pitur yaś ca na sa putraḥ satāṃ mataḥ
english: "My command was not followed by my eldest, Yadu; and he who acts contrary to his father is not considered a son by the righteous."
